newsitem.title: USA: U.S. activating 500 reserve troops for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. activating 500 reserve troops for Bosnia.

text.p: The Army is calling about 500 part-time reserve troops to active duty to train and support U.S. peacekeeping troops in Bosnia through the middle of March, the U.S. Defence Department said on Friday.

The troops will be activated from artillery and civil affairs units and most will be sent to Europe outside of Bosnia to help train a protective force of nearly 7,500 active-duty U.S. soldiers now being sent into Bosnia. That force will cover the withdrawal of 15,000 U.S. peacekeepers there.
Defence officials said the reservists would replace U.S. troops being rotated out of Bosnia.

Although the United States has made no decision to take part in any new NATO-led peacekeeping force in Bosnia next year, the Pentagon has said several thousand members of the protective U.S. force will remain in Bosnia until mid-March.
The 500 troops will be drawn from 11 National Guard and Reserve units which were notified on Friday to be prepared to supply troops in early November, the Defence Department said.

Units include a National Guard battery from the 35th Field Artillery in Hutchinson, Kansas, and the following Army Reserve units: 361st Civil Affairs Brigade, Pensacola, Florida; 411th Civil Affairs Battalion, Danbury, Connecticut; 413th Civil Affairs Battalion, Lubbock, Texas, and 431st Civil Affairs Battalion, Little Rock, Arkansas.

Also the 443rd Civil Affairs Battalion, Warwick, Rhode Island; 478th Civil Affairs Battalion, Perrine, Florida; 486th Civil Affairs Battalion, Broken Arrow, Oklahomo; 353rd Civil Affairs Command, Bronx, New York; 304th Civil Affairs Battalion, Philadeplhia, Pennsylvania and 404th Civil Affairs Battalion, Fort Dix, New Jersey.
